title.en: Responsible Data and AI Practice in the Kingdom
title.ar: الممارسة المسؤولة للبيانات والذكاء الاصطناعي في المملكة

tagline: Make one AI build lawful and responsible: map and minimise its personal data, classify and share it under the national policies, test it against the ethics principles and write its risk register and disclosure
description: Participants make one small build lawful and responsible: a parent-enquiry assistant for a fictional private school group that drafts replies from attendance and fee records with a language model. They map its personal data and minimise it under the Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL), classify each data set under the National Data Management Office (NDMO) policy, decide what may reach an external model, turn the SDAIA AI Ethics Principles into tests, assess risk with the National AI Risk Management Framework, and write the disclosure and records the build needs.
audience: Beginners. Graduates and career changers entering the AI Engineering or Data Science track; computing and data graduates who pass the placement test skip the courses it covers.
prerequisites: FN-101 Python for Data and AI Work
FN-105 How Machine Learning and Language Models Work
Reads a short Python program that calls a web API

outcomes.text: Explain the PDPL obligations that govern a build, from lawful basis and minimisation to rights, retention, transfer and breach handling, given the assistant's data flow diagram
outcomes.evidence: an annotated diagram naming the obligation at each step, checked against the reference

outcomes.text: Distinguish what the data classification, data sharing and open data policies and the SDAIA Generative AI Guidelines each decide, given six questions about the build
outcomes.evidence: a decision table naming the governing instrument, matching the reference on at least five of six

outcomes.text: Classify each data set of the build under the four NDMO classification levels and derive the rule for sending it to an external model service, given the school group's data inventory and the policy's impact categories
outcomes.evidence: a classification register with level, reason and permitted destinations per data set

outcomes.text: Apply minimisation and pseudonymisation to the data the assistant sends, and test whether records can be re-identified, given synthetic student and guardian records
outcomes.evidence: a before-and-after field list, a pseudonymisation script and a re-identification test result

outcomes.text: Prepare a risk assessment that places the assistant in an ethics risk tier and works through the four phases of the national risk framework, given the build description and five candidate harms
outcomes.evidence: a risk register with tier, likelihood and impact ratings, an owner, a treatment and a review date per risk

outcomes.text: Test the assistant against the ethics principles for fairness across Arabic and English enquiries, transparency and human review, and draft the disclosure parents see, given forty scripted enquiries
outcomes.evidence: a test report with results per check, the changes made and the disclosure text

case_study.name: Rawafid Schools Group
case_study.summary: Rawafid Schools Group is a fictional private school group with four campuses and about 1,200 students. Its systems lead built Wafi, an assistant that drafts replies to parents from attendance and fee records with a language model, and its data protection officer must now make that build lawful and responsible. Every record is synthetic, generated with a fixed seed, and planted with the problems the labs find: a prompt that carries the whole student file, a log kept too long, linkable quasi-identifiers, a partner asking for too much, a non-commercial dataset and a routing rule that only knows English.

format_note: Intensive: 3 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task

days.title: Personal data and the law

sessions.title: Where personal data flows in a build
outcomes: Identify the personal and sensitive data a build reads, sends, logs and stores
Draw a data flow diagram of an AI assistant with every store and external party
Name the PDPL obligation that applies at each step of the flow

lab.title: Trace Wafi's personal data
lab.summary: Map every field the assistant reads, sends, logs and stores on a data flow diagram.

steps.text: Run one enquiry through the instrumented Wafi
List every field read, sent, logged and stored
Flag the identifiers and the sensitive fields
Draw the data flow diagram in Mermaid
Name the PDPL obligation at each step

lab.stretch: Add the hosted provider's own logs as a store you do not control

sessions.summary: Prompts, logs, caches and the model provider are all places where personal data goes

sessions.title: Lawful basis and minimisation
outcomes: Choose a legal basis and a purpose for each flow of a build
Test each field against the purpose and remove what it does not need
Rewrite a prompt builder so it sends the minimum

lab.title: Lawful basis and minimum fields
lab.summary: Set a lawful basis and purpose for each flow and remove the fields the purpose does not need.

steps.text: Set a basis and purpose for each of the five flows
Test each prompt field against the purpose
Write the minimised prompt builder
Check ten prompts and print the before-and-after list

lab.stretch: Draft the consent wording for the one optional flow

sessions.summary: Every flow needs a legal basis and a purpose, and every field must earn its place against that purpose

sessions.title: Pseudonymisation and its limits
outcomes: Pseudonymise identifiers with a keyed hash and keep the key apart
Attempt re-identification by joining on quasi-identifiers
Generalise quasi-identifiers and measure the remaining risk

lab.title: Pseudonymise, then attack
lab.summary: Pseudonymise the guardian and student records and attempt to re-identify them by linkage.

steps.text: Replace identifiers with keyed pseudonyms
Join with the sports-day page on quasi-identifiers
Measure the re-identification rate
Generalise birth date and grade, measure again
Record k and the residual risk

lab.stretch: Show that an unkeyed hash of a student number is reversed by trying every number

sessions.summary: A pseudonym hides a name, not a person: quasi-identifiers link records back

sessions.title: Rights, retention and breaches
outcomes: Explain the data subject's rights and who exercises them for a minor
Write a retention rule per store and find what is kept too long
Walk a breach through notice, containment and documentation

lab.title: Retention and a seeded breach
lab.summary: Write a retention rule per store and walk a seeded breach through the PDPL breach guideline.

steps.text: Write a retention rule per store
Count log rows past the rule
Read the incident and size the breach
Draft the notice to SDAIA with its five contents
Decide the notice to guardians

lab.stretch: Add the breach to the documentation record with its corrective actions

sessions.summary: Rights, retention rules and the breach procedure turn the law into dates and duties

days.subtitle: Map, justify, minimise, pseudonymise and keep the data of one build

days.title: Classify, share and send

sessions.title: Data classification levels
outcomes: Assess the impact category and level of a data set's disclosure
Assign a classification level with an evidence-based reason
Spot aggregates that still reveal individuals

lab.title: Classify six data sets
lab.summary: Classify the six data sets with the policy's impact categories and record the reasons.

steps.text: Read the inventory and the impact categories
Assess impact category and level per set
Map impact to level and sub-level
Find the small cells in the aggregate table
Record reasons in the register

lab.stretch: Suppress the small cells and classify the aggregate table again

sessions.summary: Classification follows the impact of disclosure: four levels, and sub-levels inside Restricted

sessions.title: What may reach an external model
outcomes: Derive a destination rule from the classification level and the data's nature
Apply the rule to data sets and to the fields of a prompt
Recognise a hosted endpoint abroad as a transfer outside the Kingdom

lab.title: Hosted, local or neither
lab.summary: Decide for each data set whether it may go to a hosted model, a locally served model or neither.

steps.text: Write the destination rule as a function
Apply it to the six data sets
Apply it field by field to Wafi's prompt
Check the hosted endpoint's location as a transfer
Record the permitted destinations

lab.stretch: Write the rule for the synthetic class data and say why it differs

sessions.summary: The classification level decides whether data may go to a hosted model, a locally served one, or neither

sessions.title: Sharing with another entity
outcomes: Assess a data request against the Data Sharing Policy principles
Cut a request down to the minimum data its purpose needs
Draft the conditions under which data may be shared

lab.title: A partner's data request
lab.summary: Assess a partner entity's request for attendance data against the Data Sharing Policy and draft the conditions.

steps.text: Read the request against the eight principles
Mark each requested field needed or not
Draft the conditions of sharing
Build the minimised extract
Check the extract for small groups

lab.stretch: Write the destruction confirmation the partner signs

sessions.summary: A request to share data is judged on purpose, minimum data, access, transparency and destruction

sessions.title: Licences and provenance
outcomes: Read the licence of a model and of a dataset from its card
Record use restrictions and obligations in a licence register
Name the national instrument that decides a given question

lab.title: Licences and provenance
lab.summary: Check the licences of two candidate open-weight models and one dataset and record the use restrictions.

steps.text: Read two model cards and one dataset card
Record licence, SPDX identifier and obligations
Decide fit for Wafi per artefact
Answer six questions with the instrument that decides

lab.stretch: Trace where the dataset's text came from and what that adds

days.subtitle: Classify each data set, decide where it may go, and check what you reuse

days.title: Ethics and risk in practice

sessions.title: Principles into tests
outcomes: Translate an ethics principle into a measurable check
Set a threshold and a pass rule for each check
Run checks over a recorded run and read the failures

lab.title: Three checks
lab.summary: Write three checks that turn fairness, transparency and accountability into pass or fail results.

steps.text: Turn fairness into a measurable check with a threshold
Turn transparency into a check on every reply
Turn accountability into a check on the log
Run all three on the recorded run

lab.stretch: Add a fourth check for privacy: no identifier in any reply

sessions.summary: A principle becomes useful when it is a check with a threshold that passes or fails

sessions.title: Testing the assistant
outcomes: Run a scripted test set through an assistant
Compare reply quality and escalation rates per language
Name the bias types that explain a measured gap

lab.title: Forty enquiries
lab.summary: Run forty scripted enquiries in Arabic and English, compare reply quality and escalation rates, and name the bias types from the national guide that explain any gap.

steps.text: Run the forty enquiries through Wafi
Score reply quality per language
Compare escalation rates per language
Name the bias types that explain the gaps
Write the test report rows

lab.stretch: Rerun with the Arabic keywords added and measure the change

sessions.summary: Paired enquiries in Arabic and English show whether the assistant serves both groups equally

sessions.title: Risk tier and risk register
outcomes: Place an AI system in an ethics risk tier with reasons
Rate harms by likelihood and impact and compute the risk level
Write a register entry with treatment, owner and review date

lab.title: Tier and register
lab.summary: Place the assistant in a risk tier and rate five harms by likelihood and impact.

steps.text: Place Wafi in an ethics risk tier with reasons
Rate five harms by likelihood and impact
Compute levels and bands
Choose a treatment, owner and review date per harm
Rate the residual risk again

lab.stretch: Change one fact (replies sent without review) and redo the tier

sessions.title: Disclosure and human review
outcomes: Draft a disclosure that names the assistant, the data and the human route
Write a rule that sends sensitive replies to staff
Test the rule for recall in both languages

lab.title: Notice and routing rule
lab.summary: Draft the notice parents see and the rule that sends sensitive replies to staff.

steps.text: Draft the notice parents see
Check it against the required items
Write the routing rule for sensitive replies
Test the rule on the forty enquiries per language
Choose your capstone build

lab.stretch: Write the Arabic notice and check both say the same

sessions.summary: Parents are told what the assistant is and does, and sensitive replies go to a person

days.subtitle: Turn the principles into tests, rate the risks and tell parents the truth

days.title: Capstone: the responsible build pack
days.subtitle: Ten-minute reviews: six minutes to present the pack, four for the assessor's changed fact

capstone.summary: A responsible build pack for the assistant or the participant's own build (registers, minimisation code with its re-identification test, ethics test report, a record of processing entry, a breach checklist and the disclosure), submitted as a public repository and defended in a ten-minute review
capstone.submission: A public GitHub repository holding the build pack: the classification and risk registers, the minimisation and pseudonymisation code with its re-identification test, the ethics test report, a record of processing entry, a breach checklist and the disclosure, with a README that links each part. Then a ten-minute review in which the assessor changes one fact of the case and the participant revises the classification and risk entries live.

a small open-weight model served locally, for real data (not used in the labs)
